x: Indian Polity: Organs of the State PMF IAS IP – 48 Both statements are correct: Article 59 states that the President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a State Legislature; if a sitting member is elected President, their seat is deemed vacant upon assuming office. x: The provision for the representation of the Anglo-Indian community in the Lok Sabha was made under Article 331 of the Constitution. According to this Article, even though provisions were made in Article 81, if the President was of the opinion that the Anglo-Indian community was not adequately represented in the Lok Sabha, he could nominate two members of that community to the Lok Sabha. According to Article 334, this provision was made initially for a period of 10 years in the Constitution. Later, it was extended for periods of 10 years each. Through the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, Article 334 was amended to extend the provision of reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for another 10 years (80 years from the commencement of the Constitution). However, the provision for the representation of Anglo-Indians was not extended further and was terminated.

x: 'Office of profit' is not defined in the Constitution or the RPA; exempted posts are listed in the 1959 Act.

s: Which case held that the Speaker's decisions under the Tenth Schedule are subject to judicial review?
x: Kihoto Hollohan (1992) upheld the Speaker's or Chairman's role in defection cases, subject to judicial review.

s: What happens if a person elected to two seats in the Lok Sabha does not choose one?
x: A member elected to two seats in one House must choose one; otherwise both seats fall vacant.

s: Under Article 103, who decides a question of disqualification of an MP (other than under the Tenth Schedule)?
o: Election Commission, after consulting the President
Supreme Court, on a reference by the President
Speaker or Chairman of the House concerned
President, acting on the opinion of the Election Commission
x: Under Article 103, the President decides the question after obtaining the opinion of the Election Commission and acts according to that opinion.

s: A person elected to both Houses of Parliament does not choose one within 10 days. In which House does he lose his seat?
o: House he was elected to first
x: If he does not choose within 10 days, his Rajya Sabha seat falls vacant; for Parliament plus a State the limit is 14 days.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The seat of a Member of Parliament falls vacant as soon as he incurs a disqualification under Article 102.
2. The House must pass a resolution before such a seat falls vacant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Under Article 101(3)(a) the seat becomes vacant immediately on disqualification; no decision of the House is needed.

s: The 106th Constitutional Amendment reserves what share of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies?
x: The 106th Amendment reserves one-third of the seats, not one-half, under Article 334A.

s: The lowest representation of women, only 19 MPs, was recorded in which Lok Sabha?
x: The 6th Lok Sabha (1977) had the fewest women members, only 19 MPs.

s: In which year was the first Women's Reservation Bill introduced?
x: The first Bill came in 1996 and was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010; the 106th Amendment was enacted in 2023.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 15th Lok Sabha — 2009 — Women crossed 10 per cent for the first time
x: The 106th Constitutional Amendment providing one-third reservation for women was enacted in 2023, not 2010. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Which Lok Sabha recorded the highest number of women members, 78?
x: The 17th Lok Sabha (2019) had 78 women (14.36%), the highest; the 18th (2024) has 74.

s: Under which Article is the women's reservation of the 106th Amendment provided?
x: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam reserves one-third seats under Article 334A for 15 years, after the next Census and delimitation.

s: In which year did the Rajya Sabha pass the Women's Reservation Bill?
x: The first Bill came in 1996, it was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010, and the 106th Amendment came in 2023.

s: What is the approximate share of women in the present Lok Sabha?
x: The 18th Lok Sabha (2024) has 74 women members, about 13.6 per cent (roughly 14 per cent). One-third is the future reservation under the 106th Amendment (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023).

s: For how many years will the women's reservation under the 106th Amendment (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) be in force?
x: The 106th Amendment (2023) reserves one-third of seats in the LS and Assemblies for 15 years, after the next Census and delimitation.

s: How many women members were there in the First Lok Sabha (1952)?
x: The 1st Lok Sabha had 22 women; the 6th had the lowest (19) and the 17th the highest (78).

s: Which Article allows the business of Parliament to be transacted in Hindi or English?
x: Article 120 recognises Hindi and English and lets a member use his mother tongue with the presiding officer's permission.

s: What is the maximum gap allowed between two sessions of Parliament?
x: Two sessions cannot be more than six months apart; this keeps legislative business going and the government accountable, though it fixes no minimum sitting days.

s: Under which Article are the rules of procedure and conduct of business in Parliament made?
x: Article 118 empowers each House to make rules for regulating its procedure and conduct of business.

s: Under which Article does the President summon each House of Parliament, with the maximum gap between two sessions limited to six months?
x: Under Article 85, the President summons each House, and no more than six months may pass between sessions. Article 123 is about ordinances.

s: Under whose control does the Rajya Sabha Secretariat function?
x: The parliamentary Secretariats are independent of the executive: the Rajya Sabha Secretariat is under the Chairman and the Lok Sabha Secretariat under the Speaker.

s: Parliament in India normally holds which three sessions in a year?
x: There is no fixed constitutional calendar, but Parliament normally has Budget, Monsoon and Winter sessions.

s:
Arrange in the correct procedural sequence after the business of a session concludes:
1. Prorogation by the President
2. Adjournment sine die by the Speaker or Chairman
3. Reassembly in a new session
4. Recess
x: The Speaker or Chairman first adjourns the House sine die, the President then prorogues it, a recess follows and the House reassembles in a new session.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: A sitting is a daily meeting of the House during a session.
Prorogation terminates the House itself but not its session.
Dissolution ends the life of the House and applies only to the Lok Sabha.
Adjournment terminates a sitting for a specified period.
x: Prorogation ends the session, not the House; only dissolution ends the House, and only the Lok Sabha can be dissolved.

s: What is the termination of a session of a House, without ending the life of the House, called?
x: Prorogation ends the session; adjournment ends a sitting for a set time, adjournment sine die ends it without a date, and dissolution ends the House.

s: During a recess of Parliament, under which Article may the President promulgate ordinances?
x: A recess is the gap between prorogation and the next session, and the President can issue ordinances under Article 123 during it.

s: The quorum for conducting official business in a House of Parliament is what fraction of its total membership?
x: Under Article 100, the quorum is one-tenth of the House's total membership.

s: Under which Article was the resolution to remove Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, rejected by voice vote on 11 March 2026, moved?
x: The removal resolution against Speaker Om Birla was moved under Article 94(c) and rejected by voice vote on 11 March 2026.

s: How many minimum sitting days a year does the Constitution prescribe for Parliament?
x: Article 85 fixes only the six-month maximum gap between sessions; it prescribes no minimum number of sitting days.

s: Which House can be dissolved?
x: Dissolution ends the House and applies only to the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha is permanent.

s: Which Article protects the freedom of speech of members in Parliament?
x: Article 105 bars court proceedings for anything said or any vote given in Parliament or its committees; it does not cover statements made outside.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sita Soren case (2024)?
o: It was decided by a seven-judge Bench.
It held that privilege does not protect a legislator who takes a bribe to vote or speak.
It held that every speech made by a legislator outside the House is protected by Article 105.
It overruled the protection recognised in P.V. Narasimha Rao (1998) on this point.
x: Sita Soren held no such thing; it held that parliamentary privilege does not protect bribery for voting or speaking.

s: What kind of privilege is the right to be informed of a member's arrest, detention or release?
o: an individual privilege of the member
a Fundamental Right of the member under Article 22
a collective privilege of the House
a privilege of the Presiding Officer alone
x: Being informed of a member's arrest, detention or release is a collective privilege of the House.

s: Besides members, to whom do parliamentary privileges also extend?
x: Privileges extend to ministers, the Attorney-General and others who speak in the House; the House also has collective privileges.

s: Under Article 122, on what ground can courts not inquire into parliamentary proceedings?
x: Article 122 bars courts from questioning parliamentary proceedings on the ground of alleged procedural irregularity.

s: Besides the session, for what period does a Member of Parliament enjoy freedom from arrest in civil cases?
x: The privilege covers civil arrest during the session and forty days before and after it; it does not cover criminal cases or preventive detention.

s: Under which Article do parliamentary privileges in India, which remain uncodified, continue?
x: Parliamentary privileges have not been comprehensively codified; they continue under Article 105(3), historically based on those of the British House of Commons.

s: Which one of the following is NOT an individual parliamentary privilege of a member?
o: Freedom from arrest in civil cases during the prescribed period
Freedom of speech in the House
Power to prohibit publication of the House's proceedings
x: The power to publish or prohibit publication of the House's reports and proceedings is a collective privilege of the House, not an individual privilege.

s: The Sita Soren judgment (2024) overruled which earlier decision on bribery and privilege?
x: A seven-judge Bench in Sita Soren (2024) held there is no privilege for a bribe to vote or speak, overruling P.V. Narasimha Rao (1998).

s: Which of the following is NOT a collective privilege of a House of Parliament?
o: Being informed of a member's arrest
x: Exemption from jury service is an individual privilege of members; the others belong to the House collectively.

s: Under Article 105(3), the uncodified privileges of the Houses of Parliament were historically those of which body?
x: Article 105(3) privileges are not codified; historically they were those of the British House of Commons.

s: Without whose approval can no tax be imposed?
x: No tax can be levied without Lok Sabha approval; questions and motions are other tools of control over the executive.

s: In the case of which Bills are the powers of the Rajya Sabha restricted?
x: The Rajya Sabha has equal powers on Constitutional Amendment Bills and can introduce Ordinary and Amendment Bills; it is restricted only for Money Bills.

s: Which of the following is correct about a Financial Bill of category I?
o: Can be introduced in either House of Parliament
Can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha
Can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and both Houses have equal powers in its passage
Can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha must return it within 14 days
x: A Financial Bill of category I can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, but unlike a Money Bill both Houses have equal powers in its passage.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Demands for grants — Rajya Sabha may vote on them
Money Bill — Rajya Sabha to return it within fourteen days
Joint sitting — Presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
x: The Rajya Sabha may discuss the Budget but cannot vote on demands for grants. A Money Bill is returned within fourteen days, a joint sitting is presided over by the Lok Sabha Speaker, and a no-confidence motion is moved in the Lok Sabha.

s: On which of the following matters do the two Houses of Parliament NOT have equal powers?
o: Passing a resolution to discontinue a National Emergency
Approval of an Ordinance promulgated by the President
Removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court
x: Only the Lok Sabha can pass a resolution to discontinue a National Emergency; the Houses are equal on the other three.

s: Which one of the following matters is within the equal powers of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha?
o: Initiation of a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers
Consideration of the report of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
x: Both Houses have equal powers in considering the reports of the CAG, UPSC and Finance Commission. The other matters are associated with the superiority of the Lok Sabha.

s: In the Budget process, which of the following can the Rajya Sabha NOT do?
o: Make recommendations on a Money Bill
x: The Rajya Sabha may discuss the Budget but cannot vote on demands for grants, which is a Lok Sabha power.

s: Which of the following can be done only by the Lok Sabha?
x: Only the Lok Sabha can discontinue a National Emergency; both Houses approve emergencies and take part in impeachment and removal of judges.

s: If the Rajya Sabha approves a National Emergency while the Lok Sabha is dissolved, within how many days of its first sitting must the new Lok Sabha approve it?
x: The Rajya Sabha may approve the proclamation for the time being; the newly constituted Lok Sabha must approve it within thirty days of its first sitting.

s: Under which Article can the Rajya Sabha authorise the creation of new All-India Services?
x: Article 312 covers new All-India Services; 249 deals with State List legislation in the national interest and 67(b) with initiating the Vice-President's removal.

s: By what majority must a Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 be supported?
o: a simple majority of members present and voting
two-thirds of members present and voting
a majority of the total membership
x: It needs two-thirds of members present and voting, is valid for one year and can be renewed one year at a time.

s: Under which Article can a proceeding to remove the Vice-President be started only in the Rajya Sabha?
x: Under Article 67(b) a resolution to remove the Vice-President can begin only in the Rajya Sabha.

s: For how long does a Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 remain in force?
o: Until the Lok Sabha is dissolved
x: An Article 249 resolution is valid for one year and can be renewed one year at a time.

s: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 authorises which body to make laws on a State List subject?
x: Article 249 empowers Parliament, not State Assemblies, to legislate on a State List matter in the national interest.

s: Which one of the following is NOT an electoral function of Parliament?
o: Participating in the election of the President
Electing the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
x: A is the answer: Parliament's electoral functions are electing the Vice-President, taking part in the President's election and electing its presiding officers (the Lok Sabha elects the Speaker and Deputy Speaker). The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President, not elected by Parliament, so A is not an electoral function.

s: Which Article deals with the procedure for impeachment of the President?
x: Impeachment is under Article 61; Article 109 covers the Rajya Sabha's 14 days on Money Bills and 90(c) the Deputy Chairman's removal.

s: Who alone can change an existing law made by Parliament?
x: Only Parliament can change an existing law it has made (APPSC-GS 2024); it legislates on the Union and Concurrent Lists and reviews delegated legislation.

s: Which of the following is a judicial function of Parliament?
x: Impeachment of the President, removal of the Vice-President, recommending removal of judges and punishing breach of privilege are Parliament's judicial functions.

s: On whose recommendation can a Bill under Article 3 to form a new State be introduced in Parliament?
x: Such a Bill needs the President's recommendation; the State Legislature's views are sought but are not binding on Parliament.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: A notice for the President's impeachment requires the signatures of at least one-fourth of the members.
Failure to resign the State Legislature seat within 14 days results in vacation of the Parliament seat.
Notice for removal of the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman requires 30 days.
A Money Bill is deemed to have been passed by the Rajya Sabha if it is not returned within 14 days.
x: Option C is incorrect: the notice for removing the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman is 14 days, not 30. Impeachment notice also needs one-fourth of members' signatures and 14 days.

s: Under which Article does Parliament make a law for two or more States on the resolutions of their legislatures?
x: Under Article 252 Parliament legislates for consenting States; other States may adopt that law later.

s: Under which Article can Parliament legislate on any subject to implement international treaties?
x: Article 253 lets Parliament make laws to implement international treaties and agreements.

s: The Rajya Sabha elects which of its presiding officers?
x: The Rajya Sabha elects only its Deputy Chairman; the Vice-President is its ex officio Chairman.

s: A notice to impeach the President must be signed by at least what fraction of the members of the House?
x: The impeachment notice must be signed by one-fourth of the members and given 14 days in advance.

s: Under which Article can Parliament make laws on a State List subject while a Proclamation of National Emergency is in operation?
x: Article 250 lets Parliament legislate on State List matters during a National Emergency; Article 249 needs a Rajya Sabha resolution.

s: Under the proposal to enlarge the Lok Sabha by about 50% once the 1971 freeze lifts, to about what number would its strength rise?
x: Raising the Lok Sabha by about 50% after the 1971 freeze would take it to about 815 seats; the 15% cap on the Council of Ministers would then rise from 81 to 122.

s: What happened to the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha?
o: It was passed with the special majority
It was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee
It was defeated, short of the special majority
x: The Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha because it did not secure the special majority needed for a constitutional amendment.

s: At what strength did the Tamil Nadu Assembly resolution on Lok Sabha delimitation seek to freeze the Lok Sabha?
x: The Tamil Nadu Assembly resolved to retain the Lok Sabha at 543 seats and preserve the approximate 2.2:1 Lok Sabha–Rajya Sabha ratio.

s: If the Lok Sabha were enlarged by about 50%, to about what would the Lok Sabha-to-Rajya Sabha ratio change from 2.2:1?
x: Raising the Lok Sabha to about 815 would push the ratio with the Rajya Sabha from 2.2:1 to 3.3:1.

s: With an enlarged Lok Sabha of about 815, to about what number would the 15% cap on the Council of Ministers rise from 81?
x: The 15% ministerial cap would rise from 81 to about 122.

s: To what number did the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 propose to raise the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha?
x: The Bill proposed raising the LS maximum from 550 to 850 (815 States, 35 UTs); it was defeated in the Lok Sabha.

s: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the Constitution of India?
x: The Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and Council of Ministers are constitutional; the post of Deputy PM is not in the Constitution.
